Uninstrumented reproduction: production g4_q4_matvec and the actual phase-62 emitter source, both options nil; both final Float bit patterns are recorded and compared before any instrumented kernel runs.

Instrumented kernels are copies with trace stores, never the originals. A trace variant is attributed to the originals only if the production-shaped trace final equals the uninstrumented control bits AND the register-shaped trace final equals the uninstrumented candidate bits; otherwise the original cause is NOT ESTABLISHED and the trace is reported as altered arithmetic.
The split variant (named w, d*w, (d*w)*x, sum) is altered arithmetic by construction; the sum-only variant keeps the two production term lines verbatim but still adds stores.

CPU accumulation models are consistent-with hypotheses on one 64-term row; a match is not a proof of the compiled instruction sequence. Both originals are compiled with options nil, the SDK default math mode, which this diagnostic does not change; the four models do not cover other permitted rewrites, so a no-match is not evidence either way.

v2 (hardened after independent review): only the sum-only trace can establish a first divergence, and only when each trace final equals its uninstrumented original, each last traced sum equals its own final, both integer unpack copies equal the host bytes, the uninstrumented outputs are finite, in contract and guard-intact, and every trace run is completed, finite, fully written and guard-intact. Final calibration is necessary, not sufficient: it is trace evidence about the calibrated copies and never proves the originals' unobservable intermediates or instruction sequence. The split trace never attributes. Every instrumented copy is checked line-for-line against the uniquely extracted original before any dispatch.

No fast-math, fma or volatile flag is applied to make either original pass; options nil selects the Metal compiler default (not the safe math mode), under which contraction and reassociation are permitted in both originals and in every instrumented copy; no timing is measured.
